# Form 16 Explained: What It Is, How Employers Generate It, and How Employees Use It for ITR Filing (2026 Guide)


October 15, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/form-16-explained-what-it-is-how-employers-generate-it-and-how-employees-use-it-for-itr-filing-2026-guide/#respond)


Every salaried employee in India has heard of Form 16. It arrives once a year from your employer, usually between May and June, and it holds the key to filing your income tax return without confusion. Yet most people either stuff it in a drawer or glance at it once and forget what half the numbers mean.


On the employer side, things are equally confusing. Small business owners often wonder how to generate Form 16, what Part A and Part B actually contain, and what happens if they miss the deadline.


This guide breaks down everything about Form 16 for both employers and employees. Whether you are a business owner trying to issue Form 16 correctly or a salaried professional preparing to file your ITR for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), you will find clear, actionable answers here.


## What Is Form 16?


Form 16 is a TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) certificate that your employer issues to you. It certifies that tax was deducted from your salary during the financial year and deposited with the government.


Think of it this way: when your employer pays you salary every month, they deduct income tax before paying you. Form 16 is the official receipt proving that deducted tax actually reached the Income Tax Department.


Detail Description


Full Name Certificate under Section 203 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 for TDS on Salary


Issued By Employer (Deductor)


Issued To Employee (Deductee)


Covers TDS deducted from salary under Section 192


Frequency Once per financial year


Deadline June 15 of the following financial year


Mandatory For Every employer who deducts TDS from salary


Governed By Rule 31 of the Income Tax Rules


Form 16 is issued under Section 203 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, read with Rule 31 of the Income Tax Rules. Every employer who deducts TDS from an employee’s salary under Section 192 must issue this certificate.


**Important:** If your employer did not deduct any TDS during the year (because your income was below the taxable limit), they are not legally required to issue Form 16. However, many employers issue it anyway as a salary summary document.


## Form 16 Has Two Parts: Part A and Part B


This is where most confusion begins. Form 16 is not a single document. It has two distinct parts, each serving a different purpose and generated from a different source.


### Quick Comparison: Part A vs Part B


Feature Part A Part B


What it contains TDS deducted and deposited details Salary breakup and tax computation


Who generates it Downloaded from TRACES portal Prepared by the employer


Source of data Government records Employer’s payroll records


Unique identification Has a unique certificate number No separate certificate number


Can be verified independently Yes, on TRACES No, employer’s own calculation


Covers multiple employers Separate Part A from each employer Separate Part B from each employer


Format Standardized by the government Standardized but filled by employer


### Part A: The Government’s Record


Part A is the official TDS certificate. It is downloaded by your employer from the TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) portal. This part contains information that the government already has on record.


**What Part A Shows:**


Field What It Tells You


Employer’s TAN Tax Deduction Account Number of your employer


Employer’s PAN Permanent Account Number of the company


Employee’s PAN Your PAN number


Assessment Year The AY for which the certificate is valid


Period of Employment Start and end date with this employer


Summary of Tax Deducted Quarter wise TDS amounts


Summary of Tax Deposited Challan details, BSR codes, dates of deposit


Certificate Number Unique number for verification


**Quarter wise TDS Breakup in Part A:**


Quarter Period TDS Deducted (Example for ₹10 LPA)


Q1 April to June ₹15,000


Q2 July to September ₹15,000


Q3 October to December ₹15,000


Q4 January to March ₹15,000


**Total** **Full Year** **₹60,000**


The most important thing about Part A is that every number in it can be verified. The certificate number printed on Part A can be checked on the TRACES portal to confirm that the TDS was actually deposited with the government.


### Part B: The Employer’s Calculation


Part B is where the actual salary details and tax computation live. Your employer prepares this part based on their payroll records. It shows how they calculated your taxable income and arrived at the TDS amount.


**What Part B Contains:**


Section Details Included


Gross Salary Basic, HRA, Special Allowance, Bonus, and all other salary components


Exemptions Claimed HRA exemption (Section 10(13A)), LTA (Section 10(5)), Standard Deduction


Income from Salary Gross Salary minus exemptions


Other Income Reported Income from house property, other sources declared to employer


Gross Total Income Total of all income heads


Deductions under Chapter VI-A Section 80C, 80D, 80E, 80CCD, and other deductions


Total Taxable Income After all deductions


Tax Computed Based on applicable tax slab (Old or New Regime)


Relief under Section 89 If applicable for salary arrears


Net Tax Payable After rebate (Section 87A) and relief


TDS Deducted Actual TDS deducted during the year


## Understanding Part B with a Real Salary Example


Let us walk through a complete Part B calculation for a typical salaried employee earning ₹10,00,000 CTC under the New Tax Regime for FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27).


### Step 1: Salary Breakup


Component Annual Amount


Basic Salary ₹4,80,000


HRA ₹2,40,000


Special Allowance ₹1,56,000


Employer PF Contribution (12% of Basic) ₹57,600


Employer ESI (if applicable) ₹0 (CTC exceeds ESI limit)


Gratuity (4.81% of Basic) ₹23,088


Medical Insurance (Group Policy) ₹10,000


Annual Bonus ₹33,312


**Total CTC** **₹10,00,000**


### Step 2: Gross Salary (as shown in Part B)


Item Amount


Basic Salary ₹4,80,000


HRA ₹2,40,000


Special Allowance ₹1,56,000


Annual Bonus ₹33,312


**Gross Salary** **₹9,09,312**


Note: Employer PF, Gratuity, and Insurance are CTC components but are not part of Gross Salary shown in Form 16.


### Step 3: Exemptions and Deductions (New Tax Regime)


Deduction Amount Applicable in New Regime?


Standard Deduction (Section 16(ia)) ₹75,000 Yes


Professional Tax (Section 16(iii)) ₹2,500 Yes


HRA Exemption (Section 10(13A)) ₹0 No (not available in new regime)


Section 80C (PF, LIC, ELSS) ₹0 No (not available in new regime)


Section 80D (Health Insurance) ₹0 No (not available in new regime)


Employer NPS (Section 80CCD(2)) ₹0 Yes (if applicable)


**Total Deductions** **₹77,500**


### Step 4: Tax Calculation (New Regime, AY 2026-27)


Taxable Income Slab Rate Tax


Up to ₹4,00,000 0% ₹0


₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 5% ₹20,000


₹8,00,001 to ₹8,31,812 10% ₹3,181


**Total Tax** **₹23,181**


Add: Cess (4%) ₹927


**Total Tax Payable** **₹24,108**


Less: Section 87A Rebate ₹0 (income exceeds ₹7 lakh threshold with marginal relief for new regime)


**Net Tax Payable** **₹24,108**


**Taxable Income Calculation:** Gross Salary (₹9,09,312) minus Standard Deduction (₹75,000) minus Professional Tax (₹2,500) = ₹8,31,812


### New Tax Regime Slabs for AY 2026-27


Income Slab Tax Rate


Up to ₹4,00,000 Nil


₹4,00,001 to ₹8,00,000 5%


₹8,00,001 to ₹12,00,000 10%


₹12,00,001 to ₹16,00,000 15%


₹16,00,001 to ₹20,00,000 20%


₹20,00,001 to ₹24,00,000 25%


Above ₹24,00,000 30%


**Note:** Under the new tax regime, income up to approximately ₹12,75,000 is effectively tax free due to the Section 87A rebate (₹60,000 rebate for income up to ₹12,00,000 with marginal relief). Standard deduction of ₹75,000 brings the effective zero tax threshold to ₹12,75,000.


## Who Is Eligible to Get Form 16?


Not every working professional receives Form 16. Here is a clear breakdown:


Scenario Gets Form 16? Reason


Salaried employee with TDS deducted Yes Employer must issue under Section 203


Salaried employee, no TDS deducted (income below taxable limit) Not mandatory No TDS means no legal obligation, but many employers still issue


Freelancer or consultant No They receive Form 16A (for non-salary TDS)


Business owner drawing salary from own company Yes Company is the employer and must follow TDS rules


Contract worker (Section 194C) No Different TDS section, gets Form 16A


Employee who switched jobs mid year Yes, from each employer Each employer issues Form 16 for their employment period


Employee on deputation Yes, from the paying entity Whoever pays the salary issues Form 16


## Form 16 vs Form 16A vs Form 16B: Know the Difference


Many people confuse Form 16 with its siblings. Here is how they differ:


Feature Form 16 Form 16A Form 16B


TDS On Salary (Section 192) Non-salary income (all other sections) Sale of property (Section 194-IA)


Issued By Employer Bank, client, or any deductor Buyer of property


Issued To Employee Recipient of non-salary payment Seller of property


Frequency Once per year After each quarter or on request Per transaction


Parts Part A + Part B Single document Single document


Common Examples Monthly salary FD interest, rent, professional fees, commission When buying a house or land


Downloaded From TRACES (Part A) TRACES TRACES


**Quick memory aid:** Form 16 is for salary, 16A is for everything else except property, and 16B is specifically for property transactions.


## How Employers Generate and Issue Form 16: Complete Steps


This section is specifically for employers, HR managers, and payroll administrators. Generating Form 16 involves both Part A (from TRACES) and Part B (from your payroll system).


### Prerequisites Before You Start


Requirement Details


Valid TAN Your company’s Tax Deduction Account Number must be active


Quarterly TDS Returns Filed Form 24Q must be filed for all four quarters (Q1 to Q4)


TDS Deposited on Time All challans must reflect on TRACES


TRACES Account Deductor login must be active on tdscpc.gov.in


Employee PAN Verified PAN for each employee


Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) For downloading Part A (or use KYC validation)


### Step by Step: Downloading Part A from TRACES


Step Action Where to Do It


1 Log in to TRACES tdscpc.gov.in with TAN and password


2 Go to Downloads Click on “Downloads” from the menu bar


3 Select Form 16 Choose “Form 16” from the dropdown


4 Enter Financial Year Select FY 2025-26


5 Enter Quarter You can select All Quarters or a specific one


6 Enter Employee PAN Enter the PAN of the employee


7 Choose Authentication KYC Validation or DSC (Digital Signature)


8 Submit Request The system queues your request


9 Check Status Go to “Requested Downloads” after some time


10 Download ZIP File Download the generated file (PDF or text)


11 Convert to PDF Use the TRACES PDF converter utility if needed


12 Verify Certificate Number Each Part A has a unique certificate number for verification


**Tip:** You can download Part A for multiple employees in bulk by uploading a text file with their PAN numbers. This saves significant time if you have more than 10 employees.


### Preparing Part B


Part B is prepared by the employer using payroll data. There is no portal or government system for Part B. You create it from your own records.


Information Needed Source


Salary breakup (Basic, HRA, Allowances) Payroll register


Perquisites and profits in lieu of salary HR records


Exempt allowances claimed Employee declarations


Standard Deduction amount Fixed at ₹75,000 for FY 2025-26


Professional Tax deducted Payroll deduction records


Income from other sources Employee declaration (Form 12BB)


Deductions under Chapter VI-A Employee investment proofs


Tax regime chosen Employee declaration


Tax computed and TDS deducted Payroll TDS calculation


### Combining Part A and Part B


Method Best For


Manual (Excel template) Very small businesses with 1 to 5 employees


Payroll software auto generation Businesses with 5+ employees


CA or payroll service provider Businesses that outsource payroll


Most[payroll software](https://salarybox.in/payroll/) systems generate Part B automatically from your payroll data and merge it with Part A downloaded from TRACES, creating a single Form 16 PDF for each employee.


If you use[SalaryBox for payroll management](https://salarybox.in/) , the TDS computation and salary breakup are already calculated each month. This makes Part B preparation straightforward because all salary components,[deductions](https://salarybox.in/blog/salary-structure-in-india-components-and-tax-implications/) , and tax calculations are already recorded.


### Deadline and Penalty for Form 16


Item Detail


Deadline for FY 2025-26 June 15, 2026


Penalty for non-issuance ₹100 per day per certificate under Section 272A(2)(g)


Maximum penalty per certificate Amount of TDS deducted


Who bears the penalty The employer (deductor)


Can employee complain Yes, to the Assessing Officer


Alternative if not received Employee can still file ITR using Form 26AS and AIS


**Real scenario:** If an employer fails to issue Form 16 for an employee from whom ₹60,000 TDS was deducted, and the delay is 90 days, the penalty would be ₹100 x 90 = ₹9,000. However, the maximum cannot exceed ₹60,000 (the TDS amount). This penalty applies per employee, so for 10 employees, the exposure could be up to ₹90,000 for a 90 day delay.


### Monthly and Quarterly Timeline Leading to Form 16


When What to Do Form/Portal


7th of every month Deposit TDS deducted from salaries Challan 281 on e-filing portal


July 31 File Form 24Q for Q1 (April to June) e-filing portal


October 31 File Form 24Q for Q2 (July to September) e-filing portal


January 31 File Form 24Q for Q3 (October to December) e-filing portal


May 31 File Form 24Q for Q4 (January to March) e-filing portal


By June 15 Issue Form 16 to employees Generated from TRACES + payroll

## How Employees Use Form 16 for Filing ITR


Now let us switch to the employee’s perspective. You have received your Form 16. Here is exactly how to use it for filing your income tax return.


### Which ITR Form to Use?


Your Situation ITR Form


Only salary income and one house property ITR-1 (Sahaj)


Salary plus capital gains or multiple house properties ITR-2


Salary plus business/freelance income ITR-3


Presumptive income (small business) ITR-4 (Sugam)


Most salaried employees with only salary income and income from one house property will file ITR-1.


### Mapping Form 16 Fields to ITR-1


This table shows you exactly which number from Form 16 goes where in ITR-1:


Form 16 Part B Field Where in ITR-1 Section in ITR-1


Gross Salary (1a to 1e) Salary as per Section 17(1) B1 (Income from Salary)


Value of Perquisites (Section 17(2)) Value of Perquisites B1


Profits in lieu of salary (Section 17(3)) Profits in lieu of salary B1


Total Gross Salary Gross Salary B1


Standard Deduction (Section 16(ia)) Standard Deduction B1 (Deductions)


Professional Tax (Section 16(iii)) Professional Tax B1 (Deductions)


Income from Salary Net Salary B1 (Total)


Income from House Property Income from House Property B2


Income from Other Sources Income from Other Sources B3


Gross Total Income Gross Total Income B4


Deductions under Chapter VI-A Deductions Part C


Total Taxable Income Total Income Part D


Tax Payable Tax Computation Part D


TDS Deducted TDS claimed Taxes Paid


### Step by Step: Filing ITR Using Form 16


Step What to Do Details


1 Log in to e-filing portal incometax.gov.in with PAN and password


2 Select Assessment Year AY 2026-27 for FY 2025-26 income


3 Choose ITR Form ITR-1 for most salaried employees


4 Select Tax Regime New regime (default) or Old regime


5 Pre filled data Portal auto fills data from Form 26AS and AIS. Verify against Form 16


6 Enter Salary Details Copy from Part B of Form 16


7 Enter Deductions Copy Chapter VI-A deductions from Part B


8 Verify Tax Computation Compare with Part B calculation


9 Verify TDS Match TDS in ITR with Part A of Form 16 and Form 26AS


10 Pay Additional Tax If any shortfall, pay using Challan 280


11 Submit ITR Submit and e-verify using Aadhaar OTP, net banking, or DSC


12 Download ITR-V Save acknowledgment for your records


### Cross Verification Checklist


Before submitting your ITR, verify these numbers match across all three documents:


Field to Verify Form 16 Form 26AS AIS/TIS


Total TDS Deducted Part A (quarterly totals) Section wise TDS TDS tab


Gross Salary Part B (Gross Salary line) Income reported Income tab


Employer TAN Part A (header) TAN column TAN listed


PAN Part A (your PAN) Your PAN Your PAN


**What if numbers don’t match?** If Form 16 shows different TDS than Form 26AS, always go by Form 26AS for ITR filing, because that reflects what actually reached the government. Ask your employer to correct Form 24Q if there is a mismatch.


## What If You Did Not Receive Form 16?


Many employees, especially in small businesses, do not receive Form 16 on time or at all. Here is what you can do:


Situation What to Do


Employer delayed Form 16 Request formally in writing (email). Mention Section 203 obligation


Employer refuses to issue File a complaint with the Income Tax Officer having jurisdiction over the employer


Employer has shut down Use Form 26AS and AIS data to file ITR


Lost your Form 16 Request a duplicate from employer. Also use Form 26AS as backup


Employer never deducted TDS Form 16 is not mandatory. Calculate tax yourself and file ITR


Had multiple employers Collect Form 16 from each employer. Combine income for ITR


**Key point:** You can always file your ITR even without Form 16. The data in Form 26AS (available on TRACES and e-filing portal) and Annual Information Statement (AIS) on the e-filing portal contains all TDS information. Form 16 makes filing easier, but it is not a prerequisite.


## Form 12BB: The Declaration That Feeds Form 16


Many employees do not realize that what appears in Form 16 Part B depends heavily on what they declared through Form 12BB during the year.


### What Is Form 12BB?


Form 12BB is the investment declaration form that employees submit to their employer. It tells the employer which[deductions and exemptions](https://salarybox.in/blog/understanding-indian-payroll-tax-structure/) you plan to claim so they can calculate TDS correctly.


Form 12BB Section Declaration Impact on Form 16


House Rent Details Rent paid, landlord name, PAN (if rent exceeds ₹1 lakh/year) HRA exemption calculation in Part B


Leave Travel Allowance Travel details, bills LTA exemption in Part B


Section 80C PF, LIC, ELSS, PPF, Tuition Fees, Home Loan Principal Chapter VI-A deductions in Part B


Section 80D Health Insurance premium Medical deduction in Part B


Section 80CCD(1B) NPS contribution Additional NPS deduction in Part B


Home Loan Interest Lender name, PAN, interest certificate Loss from House Property in Part B


### Investment Proof Submission Timeline


Event Typical Deadline What Happens


Provisional Declaration April (start of FY) Employer uses declared amounts for TDS calculation


Revised Declaration October to December Employee can update declarations mid year


Proof Submission January to February Employee submits actual investment proofs


TDS Adjustment February to March Employer recalculates TDS based on actuals


Form 16 Issued By June 15 Final Form 16 reflects actual verified investments


**Common mistake:** Employees declare ₹1,50,000 under Section 80C at the start of the year but invest only ₹80,000. The employer adjusts TDS in the last quarter, leading to higher deduction in February and March. This surprises many employees and shows up clearly in the quarterly breakup of Part A.


## Old Tax Regime vs New Tax Regime in Form 16


Starting FY 2023-24, the new tax regime became the default. Your Form 16 Part B will reflect whichever regime you chose. Here is how both look in Form 16:


### Side by Side Comparison for ₹12 LPA Salary


Item Old Tax Regime New Tax Regime


Gross Salary ₹10,80,000 ₹10,80,000


Standard Deduction ₹50,000 ₹75,000


Professional Tax ₹2,500 ₹2,500


HRA Exemption ₹1,44,000 (assumed) ₹0


Section 80C ₹1,50,000 ₹0


Section 80D ₹25,000 ₹0


NPS 80CCD(1B) ₹50,000 ₹0


**Net Taxable Income** **₹6,58,500** **₹10,02,500**


Tax (before cess) ₹45,200 ₹60,250


Cess (4%) ₹1,808 ₹2,410


Section 87A Rebate ₹0 ₹0


**Total Tax** **₹47,008** **₹62,660**


Note: The calculation above uses assumed values. Actual amounts depend on your specific salary structure, rent paid, and investments made. For employees earning under ₹12,75,000, the new regime is often better because of the Section 87A rebate.


**How to check which regime your Form 16 uses:** Look at Part B. If you see deductions under Section 80C, 80D, HRA exemption, and other standard deductions, your employer computed tax under the old regime. If Part B shows only Standard Deduction and Professional Tax with no Chapter VI-A deductions (except employer NPS), you are under the new regime.

Mistake How to Spot It What to Do

## Real Scenario: Employee Who Switched Jobs Mid Year


Priya worked at Company A from April to September 2025 and joined Company B in October 2025. Here is how Form 16 works for her:


### What She Receives


From Period Covered Salary Shown TDS Deducted


Company A April 2025 to September 2025 ₹4,50,000 ₹15,000


Company B October 2025 to March 2026 ₹5,40,000 ₹22,000


**Combined** **Full Year** **₹9,90,000** **₹37,000**


### How She Files ITR


Step Action


1 Collect Form 16 from both Company A and Company B


2 Add up Gross Salary from both Part B sections


3 Check that deductions are not double claimed (Standard Deduction applies only once for ₹75,000)


4 Combine TDS from both Part A certificates


5 Verify combined TDS matches Form 26AS


6 Report full year income in one ITR


7 Claim refund if excess TDS was deducted


**Important for the second employer:** When Priya joined Company B, she should have submitted Form 12B (not 12BB) declaring her income and TDS from Company A. This helps Company B calculate TDS correctly for the remaining period. Without Form 12B, Company B treats her as if she earned nothing before October, and her total TDS for the year may be insufficient or excessive.


### TDS Mismatch Risk in Job Switching


Scenario TDS Risk What Happens


Employee declares previous income to new employer Correct TDS New employer adjusts TDS rate upward


Employee does not declare previous income Under deduction Employee owes tax at ITR filing and may face interest under Section 234B


Both employers give full basic exemption Over deduction Employee gets refund when filing ITR

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)


**1. Is Form 16 mandatory for filing income tax return?**


No, Form 16 is not mandatory for filing your ITR. You can file using data from Form 26AS and the Annual Information Statement (AIS) available on the e-filing portal. Form 16 makes the process easier because it consolidates your salary details and TDS computation in one document. But if your employer has not issued Form 16, you can still file your return by gathering salary slips, bank statements, and TDS information from Form 26AS.


**2. What is the difference between Form 16 Part A and Part B?**


Part A is the official TDS certificate downloaded from the TRACES portal. It shows quarter wise details of TDS deducted from your salary and the corresponding challan details confirming that the tax was deposited with the government. Part B is prepared by your employer and contains your complete salary breakup, exemptions claimed, deductions under Chapter VI-A, and the detailed tax computation. Part A is standardized by the government, while Part B is filled by the employer based on payroll records.


**3. Can I file ITR without Form 16 if my employer did not issue it?**


Yes. Log in to the income tax e-filing portal (incometax.gov.in) and check your Form 26AS for TDS credit details. Also check the Annual Information Statement (AIS) for a comprehensive view of your financial transactions. Use your monthly salary slips to reconstruct the salary breakup. You can file ITR with this information even if you never received Form 16.


**4. What should I do if the TDS in Form 16 does not match Form 26AS?**


Always rely on Form 26AS for filing your ITR because it reflects the TDS that actually reached the government. If there is a mismatch, contact your employer and ask them to file a correction statement (revised Form 24Q) on TRACES. Until the correction is filed and Form 26AS is updated, claim only the TDS amount shown in Form 26AS.


**5. My employer deducted TDS but did not deposit it with the government. What can I do?**


This is a serious issue. Your Form 16 may show TDS deducted, but Form 26AS will not reflect the deposit. In such cases, you should first raise the matter with your employer in writing. If the employer does not resolve it, file a complaint with the Income Tax Officer. You can also write to the TDS wing of the Income Tax Department. The employer faces penalties under Section 276B (prosecution for failure to deposit TDS) with imprisonment of 3 months to 7 years plus fine.


**6. Do I get Form 16 if I earn below the taxable limit?**


If your employer did not deduct any TDS because your income was below the taxable limit, issuing Form 16 is not legally required. However, many employers issue it as a salary certificate for the employee’s records. If you need a document proving your salary for loan applications or visa purposes, request your employer for a salary certificate or Form 16 even if no TDS was deducted.


**7. I switched two jobs this year. How do I handle two Form 16 certificates?**


You will receive separate Form 16 from each employer covering their respective employment periods. When filing ITR, add up the Gross Salary from both Part B documents. Apply Standard Deduction (₹75,000) only once, not from each Form 16. Combine TDS from both Part A certificates. Verify the total TDS against Form 26AS. Submit Form 12B to your new employer at the time of joining so they can account for your previous income while computing TDS.


**8. What is the penalty if an employer does not issue Form 16 by June 15?**


Under Section 272A(2)(g) of the Income Tax Act, the employer faces a penalty of ₹100 per day of delay for each certificate not issued. The penalty continues until the Form 16 is actually issued. However, the maximum penalty per certificate is capped at the amount of TDS deducted for that employee. For example, if TDS deducted was ₹50,000 and the delay is 200 days, the calculated penalty would be ₹20,000 (200 x ₹100). This penalty applies per employee, so for 20 employees with a 100 day delay, the total exposure could be up to ₹2,00,000.
